post.caption: Elizabeth's gold rush ended in a wall. In 1576, Martin Frobisher brought home a black stone from Baffin Island. London assayers first found nothing, then an Italian alchemist got gold. Backers sent him back, and he returned with over a hundred tons. In 1578, fifteen ships sailed for more, with Queen Elizabeth backing them. The fleet returned with more than a thousand tons of ore. Furnaces and mills rose at Dartford in Kent to extract the gold. They never found gold in the bulk of the ore. Some of the leftover rock was built into a wall at Dartford. More than 500 pieces went into that wall.
